clue.text: Temperament shown by standard thoroughbreds

parts.note: blood can mean temperament or disposition, as in hot blood or bad blood
stock means standard or usual, as in a stock answer

explanation.surface: Racehorses with the right breeding show their mettle and their pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is only a link joining the two pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodstock is the collective term for pedigree horses bred for racing.

clue.text: Vessel accommodating Chaucer's wife?

definitions.meaning: the city that was home to the Wife of ___ in The Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: A ship that has room for the wife of a medieval poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales include the Wife of Bath; Bath is an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a large vessel for bathing, and Bath is the city the Wife of Bath came from.

clue.text: It may be required, partly for a licentiateship

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a qualification for a licence may be compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue cut 'licentiateship' short; the page prints it in full. The run starts inside 'for' and ends on the L of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination is often required for a professional qualification such as a licentiateship.

clue.text: Party man without wine is brassed off

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the man's name wraps around the wine

parts.note: Ned is a man's name
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A partygoer with nothing to drink is fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'brassed off' is British slang for annoyed. TENT is an old name for a dark Spanish red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassed off is British slang for fed up or disgruntled, which is dissatisfied.

clue.text: Go round centre of big Italian city

indicators.note: round says the word for go is placed around the next piece

parts.note: a turn is a go in a game

indicators.note: the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Travel around the middle of a large city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' looks like one phrase meaning circle, but 'Go' is TURN and 'round' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, in Piedmont, is a major city of northern Italy.

clue.text: Concerned with chapter in particular unfinished novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
unfinished says the word particular loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Relating to a chapter of one novel in particular that was never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book but is the anagram signal; 'unfinished' cuts PARTICULAR to PARTICULA for the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitular relates to a cathedral chapter, the body of canons, from Latin capitulum.

clue.text: Backing for strikes produces dispute

indicators.note: backing here means turning the word for strikes so it reads from end to start

parts.note: raps are sharp blows, so to rap is to strike

explanation.surface: Support for industrial action leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' pretends to be industrial action but is the verb for hitting; 'Backing' turns RAPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or bicker, a verbal form of boxing practice.

clue.text: Flag-waving Irishman at disturbance is leader of mob

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman in crosswords
a riot is a violent public disturbance
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A banner-waving Irishman at a riot leads the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is only a link word; Pat is the crossword's stock Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is love of one's country, shown by waving its flag.

clue.text: Small part of opera catalogue absorbing a performer

indicators.note: absorbing says the two pieces take in the letter between them

parts.note: a recit, short for recitative, is a sung speech-like passage in opera
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A brief excerpt from an opera listing takes in a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small part of opera catalogue' reads as one phrase, but 'absorbing' has the two pieces take in A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist is someone who gives recitals, a solo musical performer.

clue.text: Copy published certificate be tween times

indicators.note: the word between (split across a line on the page) says the inner pieces sit inside the two outer letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so times gives one T
the plural supplies a second T to close the other end
a newspaper that ran a story published it
a script is a written document, such as a doctor's certificate or prescription

explanation.surface: A duplicate of a printed certificate is issued at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' gives two letters T, one at each end, with RAN SCRIPT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A transcript is a written copy of something, such as a record of grades or proceedings.

clue.text: Beginning to observe twitching of the ear

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so this takes the opening of observe

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: Watch out for the first sign of a twitch in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear, from Greek for ear.

clue.text: Initiating publicity for a motoring requirement

parts.note: sparking means setting off or initiating, as in sparking a debate
a plug is a piece of publicity for a product

explanation.surface: Advertising is a must for a car launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparking plug, the older name for a spark plug, ignites the fuel in a car engine.

clue.text: Draw attention to one of the field in cross-country race

parts.note: to point to something is to draw attention to it
point is a fielding position in cricket, so a fielder there is one of the field

explanation.surface: Someone in a field directs the eye towards a horse race over open country.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a cricket fielding position on the off side, close to the batsman; 'the field' is the fielding side, not a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase for hunting horses run across country.

clue.text: After a time, secures entrances

indicators.note: after says the word for secures follows the word for a time

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
to bind is to tie or secure

explanation.surface: After a while, someone locks the doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' looks like doors but is the verb, accented on the second syllable: to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to captivate or hold someone enthralled.

clue.text: Drink a monarch is brewing

indicators.note: brewing suggests the letters are being stirred up and remade

explanation.surface: A king is making a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is brewing' rearranges A MONARCH; IS joins the fodder only if read that way, so here it belongs to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a cherry liqueur from Dalmatia.

clue.text: Able to act effectively, like the theatrical Gus?

definitions.meaning: sensible and workable, suited to getting things done
Gus the Theatre Cat appears in T S Eliot's Old Possum's Book of ___ Cats

explanation.surface: An old stage cat is a capable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Gus is the ageing actor cat in T S Eliot's book of verse that inspired the musical Cats; the title calls its cats by this adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone practical is competent and down to earth, good at doing rather than theorising.

clue.text: Group of soldiers no good for Africa, say

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a contingent is a body of troops sent to join a larger force

explanation.surface: A unit of troops proves useless for service in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' reads as useless, but 'good' is G and 'no' takes it out of CONTINGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is an example of a continent, one of the earth's great landmasses.

clue.text: Charge a pound to see exotic animal

parts.note: a rate is a price or fee charged
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: It costs a pound to view a strange creature at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, an animal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Acquire knowledge? The converse, once

definitions.meaning: to pick up facts or skills by study
the opposite of acquiring knowledge is imparting it, and the word once meant to teach

explanation.surface: Is gaining wisdom the opposite of what it used to be?
explanation.walkthrough: In older and dialect English the verb meant to teach, as in 'that'll learn you'; 'once' marks the archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to gain understanding; the obsolete opposite sense is to instruct someone.

clue.text: On reflection, he made a bloomer, having fallen in love

definitions.text: On reflection, he made a bloomer, having fallen in love

parts.words: On reflection, he made a bloomer, having fallen in love
parts.note: the Greek youth who fell for his own image in a pool and was turned into a flower; a bloomer is both a blunder and a flower

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a lovestruck man admits he made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder but means a flowering plant, and 'reflection' is his image in water, not thought.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth fell in love with his reflection and became the daffodil-like flower.

clue.text: For one scientific study, trace changes in another

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for another science

parts.note: another scientific study here is biology, the study of living things

indicators.note: changes says the letters of trace are rearranged

explanation.surface: A researcher alters some figures in a second field of science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 'scientific study' for a second one; 'changes' scrambles the five letters, which sit after the opening letter of that other science.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteriology is the branch of science devoted to bacteria, a field of microbiology.

clue.text: Chap secured by line provided by a climber

indicators.note: secured by says the man's name is held between the letters around it

parts.note: Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man fastened by a rope supplied by a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a mountaineer but is a climbing plant; 'provided by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Advanced fast

definitions.meaning: money ... is advanced as a loan
the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A forward move made quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is the season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the season of abstinence before Easter, and lent is the past of lend, to advance money.

clue.text: Catch claw

definitions.meaning: to ... a criminal is to catch them
an animal's horny claw on the toe

explanation.surface: A grab with talons.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a talon or claw, and to nail someone is to catch or arrest them.

clue.text: In which some sleepers may accidentally be disturbed

definitions.text: In which some sleepers may accidentally be disturbed

parts.words: In which some sleepers may accidentally be disturbed
parts.note: sleepers are the wooden ties under railway track, and passengers asleep on a night train; both are upset when a train leaves the rails

explanation.surface: An event in which people asleep are woken by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleepers' suggests people in bed, but also means railway sleepers, the beams under the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: When a train comes off the rails, the track's sleepers and sleeping passengers alike are thrown about.

clue.text: As ordered, gathers it before noon to tidy up

indicators.note: before says the rearranged letters come ahead of the next piece
as ordered says the letters of gathers it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone collects things up before midday so as to tidy the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As ordered' rearranges the nine letters of 'gathers it', and 'before' puts them ahead of the noon letter; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a room is to put it in order, a synonym of tidying.
